Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, we can move Finlytics onto an AWS Marketplace private offer to simplify procurement and enable co-sell credits with AWS. A few items I want to confirm so we can prepare the seller-side private offer:

- Pricing band: we can apply a standard usage tier or lock a committed monthly spend with a blended discount. I can put two options in the draft (commit v. on-demand).
- Buyer approvals: who specifically needs to approve the AWS private offer in your org (procurement, legal, finance, engineering)? Also confirm the email addresses so the offer can be routed properly.

Next steps I suggest: I’ll prepare a draft private-offer PDF and a short mutual action plan (attachment) showing milestones (DocuSign request, seller acceptance, buyer sign-off, AWS acceptance). Once you confirm approvers and term, I’ll loop in our marketplace specialist to request the private offer from AWS.

Checklist for AWS Private Offer (seller deliverables)

1) 12-month committed spend: 15% discount vs list, monthly billing on marketplace.
2) 12-month prepaid (single invoice): 22% discount with AWS private-offer note for prepaid funds.
3) 36-month committed: 30% discount but requires CFO approval and longer commitment.

AWS acceptance timeline: once we submit the private-offer request and attachments, AWS usually takes 2-4 business days to process for standard cases. If buyer legal requests non-standard clauses, that can extend the cycle.

DocuSign: I can generate the DocuSign envelope after buyer confirms the pricing option. I’ll include a draft PO template and MSA excerpt in the envelope.

Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Draft.pdf (PDF - 48KB), SOC2_Type2_excerpt.pdf (PDF - 120KB)
